newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Labour Court to intervene in nurses' dispute.
newsitem.headline: Irish Labour Court to intervene in nurses' dispute.

text.p: Ireland's Labour Court said on Wednesday that it had decided to carry out a formal investigation into the dispute concerning the pay and conditions of Irish nurses.

Following exploratory discussions with health service employers and union leaders representing 26,000 nurses, the Labour Court said it had invited both parties to attend the court for a hearing at 1700 GMT on Wednesday.

The nurses have threatened to strike from Monday if their demands, which include early retirement at 55, better terms for staff nurses and those entering the profession and bonuses for those with additional qualifications, are not met.
They have already rejected a 50 million punt government offer.

Irish health minister Michael Noonan says he cannot afford any more than what is on offer and is also worried that he could trigger a further round of public sector pay claims if he meets the nurses' demands.

A strike, which would be the first ever by Irish nurses, would cause serious disruption to the Irish health service, resulting in the cancellation of routine hopsital admissions and out-patient appointments and a withdrawal from non-nursing support work and administrative duties.
